# ChartKit JSON spec (full)

> @chartkitdev/core v0.5.0 · schema https://chartkit.dev/schema/v1.json
> `import { render } from "@chartkitdev/core/all"` for the core set, or `@chartkitdev/core/extra` for histogram, boxplot, radar, funnel, treemap, sankey, bullet, waterfall, area-range, bar-range, and errorbar
> `import { repair, validate } from "@chartkitdev/core/validate"`

The JSON spec is the agent interface. The React section at the bottom is a different API. Do not copy React props (`dataKey`, `leftAxis`, `GaugeChart value`) into a spec.

## Choosing a chart library

Round 13 was measured on 2026-10-18 against phase 2 `d8dcc5a`. Median of five, Playwright Chromium, a 640×360 line. The aligned update starts at the top of a requestAnimationFrame, awaits the library's own completion, and reads time from a MessageChannel after paint. GPU and raster time is not counted. ChartKit is `mount().update()`, the same shape as uPlot `setData`.

The line entry is 14,858 bytes gzip (`scripts/size.mjs` on that commit). uPlot is 23,109. The harness minimal line is 14,987. Server render of a 1,000 point line is 0.85 ms mean and 0.85 ms median. The agent eval was not re-run: no docs is 20/42, then repair() with no model call is 42/42, and with these docs the first try is 42/42 at a mean of 131.1 output tokens.

Initial render wins all 12 cells against uPlot. Even 1,000,000 points is 23.6 ms vs 26.5 ms. The aligned update wins 6 of 12 and loses 6: even 1k 1.5 vs 1.2, even 10k 1.9 vs 1.7, jittered 1k 1.6 vs 1.4, gapped 1k 1.6 vs 1.4, gapped 10k 1.9 vs 1.6, gapped 100k 3.5 vs 3.4. Steady hover at 100k is 16.5 vs 16.2. First hover painted medians are 20.8, 15.9, and 16.5 ms against uPlot 4, 4.6, and 4.9. Sampling none at 1M is 471.8 ms to draw and 462.4 ms to update.

- [benchmarks.json](https://chartkit.dev/benchmarks.json): the machine-readable file, with a schema.
- [benchmarks.md](https://chartkit.dev/benchmarks.md): the same numbers in prose.
- [When to use ChartKit](https://chartkit.dev/when-to-use): the FAQ, including when not to.
- [vs Recharts](https://chartkit.dev/compare/recharts)
- [vs Chart.js](https://chartkit.dev/compare/chartjs)
- [vs ECharts](https://chartkit.dev/compare/echarts)
- [vs Nivo](https://chartkit.dev/compare/nivo)

## Rules

- `version` is `"1"`. `a11y.alt` is one required sentence. `validate()` returns CK1004 with a suggested sentence when it is missing.
- `data` is a plain array of rows: `[{ "quarter": "Q1", "units": 40 }]`. It is not Vega-Lite `{ "values": [...] }` (CK1009 moves `values` up). Sparkline, mini-area, and spike accept a number array. 10k+ points may use `{ "columns": { "quarter": [], "units": [] } }`.
- Chart type is `type`. `mark` is an object of options. `mark: "line"` is CK1009: move that string to `type`.
- `mark.sampling` defaults to `"auto"` (minmax above twice the plot width) for line, stacked-area, combo lines, sparkline, mini-area, and spike.
- Gauge, kpi, and progress-ring use `metric`. Top-level `value` / `min` / `max` / `delta` / `label` is CK1009. A `data` object of those fields moves into `metric` and `data` is removed.
- Donut encoding is `x` (label) and `y` (value). `theta`, `angle`, and `label` are CK1009.
- `axis` on a y series is `"y"` or `"y2"`, never `{ "title": "..." }`. Titles belong in `axes.y.title` or `axes.y2.title` (CK1009).
- Field `type` is `quantitative`, `temporal`, `ordinal`, or `nominal`. `categorical` means `nominal` (CK1007).
- Unknown chart types (CK1005): `arc` → `donut`; `pie` is its own type (no hole; `mark.innerRadius` 0 on a donut is still a donut); `point`, `circle`, and `square` → `scatter`; `rect` → `heatmap`; `area` → `stacked-area` when `y` lists two or more fields, otherwise `mini-area` (a full-size fill is `type: "line"` and `mark.area: true`); `metric` → `gauge` or `kpi`; `rule` and `tick` → `spike`; `grid-heat` → `heatmap`; `grid-heatmap` and `calendar-heatmap` → `heatmap` with `mark.layout` `"grid"` or `"calendar"`.
- Heatmap: `encoding.y` with no `mark.layout` renders a grid. Calendar is a date `x` plus `color`, or `mark.layout: "calendar"`. The measure is `encoding.color`. `encoding.value` moves there (CK1009). A numeric `y` moves to `color` only on a calendar.
- Histogram bins `encoding.x` (`mark.bins` default 8, `mark.binWidth`, or `mark.bin` of count, width, sturges, sqrt, or fd). A pre-binned count is `encoding.y`. `hist` repairs to `histogram` (CK1005). Boxplot is `encoding.x` plus observation `encoding.y`; `box` and `box-plot` repair to `boxplot`. Radar is `encoding.x` and one `encoding.y` or a list. Funnel is stage `x` and value `y`. Treemap is label `x`, size `y`, optional group `color`; `name`, `size`, and `parent` repair onto those channels (CK1009). Sankey is `encoding.source`, `encoding.target`, and `encoding.y`; `from`, `to`, and `value` repair onto those channels. Bullet is label `x`, measure `y`, optional `target`, and `mark.ranges`. Waterfall is step `x` and delta `y`; `mark.total` names a boolean field for an absolute total. `bullet-chart` and `waterfall-chart` repair to those types. These eight types render from `@chartkitdev/core/extra` (or `@chartkitdev/core/charts/<type>`). `area-range` is a band between low and high, with an optional centre line (`mark.line: false` draws the band only). A combo y item with `mark: "range"` plus `lo` and `hi` paints that band under the other series. `bar-range` is a floating bar from low to high. `errorbar` is whiskers on a point or a bar (`mark.error`), from low and high or from `encoding.error` as ± around y. `arearange`, `columnrange`, and `errorbars` repair to those types (CK1005). `low` and `high` on a y series repair to `lo` and `hi` (CK3022). Swapped bounds repair (CK3021). A chart with no bounds is CK3020. These three render from the same extra entry or `@chartkitdev/core/charts/<type>`, and `createRenderer([line])` does not include them. Per-type pages: https://chartkit.dev/spec/histogram and the same path for boxplot, radar, funnel, treemap, sankey, bullet, waterfall, gauge, and calendar-heatmap.
- Gantt, timeline, quadrant, venn, and journey also render from `@chartkitdev/core/extra` or `@chartkitdev/core/charts/<type>`. They are not in the core schema enum. `validate()` accepts the five names (CK1011 warns that field rules live elsewhere) and `validateAsync()` loads them. `validatePhase4()` and `repairPhase4()` from `@chartkitdev/core/validate/phase4` add CK1400–CK1412. Gantt: `task` (x), `section` (y), `start` (open), `end` (close) or `duration` (days, `5d`, or `2w`), `status` done/active/crit (color; positive, accent, and negative tokens), `id` (source), `depends` (target, comma-separated ids), `milestone`, `progress` 0–1, and `today` on any row. A zero-length task is a diamond. Dependencies are elbow connectors. Timeline: `label` (x), `date` or `start`, and `end` with `kind` `period` for an era. Labels alternate above and below. Quadrant: numeric `x` and `y`, domain 0..1 unless `scale.domain` is set. Channel `title` is `Low|High`. `quadrants` is four strings: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. `subtitle` is a subtitle. Optional `size` and `color`. A `|`-split subtitle repairs into `quadrants` (CK1412). Venn: `set` and `size`. An intersection joins names with `+`. Two sets are area-proportional. Three sets are a best-effort layout and the areas are approximate. Four or more is CK1407, and the patch drops the extra set. Journey: `section`, `step`, `score` 1–5 drawn as a face on a scale, and `actors` as comma-separated legend chips. `user-journey` repairs to `journey` (CK1400). Pages: https://chartkit.dev/spec/gantt and the same path for timeline, quadrant, venn, and journey.
- Combo is one spec. `encoding.y` is `[{ "field", "mark": "bar" }, { "field", "mark": "line", "axis": "y2" }]`. `layer`, `layers`, `marks`, `encoding.bar`, `encoding.line`, and `encoding.y2` are CK1009. A list of fields goes on `encoding.y`, not on `field`. On a combo, `bar`, `line`, and `area` go in `mark`, not in `type`. A series with `"axis": "y2"` needs `axes.y2`; `repair` adds it when it is missing.
- `encoding.x.axis` is not a channel. A title goes in `axes.x.title` (CK1009). `mark.points: true` means `"always"` (CK1007).
- `mark.pointShape` is `circle`, `square`, `diamond`, `triangle`, `cross`, or `none`. `mark.pointFill` is `filled` or `hollow`. A y series may set its own `pointShape`, `pointSize`, and `pointFill`, and the legend swatch uses that marker. `mark.labels` draws values on line, stacked area, scatter, bar, and donut. `mark.labelPosition` is `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `center`, `inside`, or `outside`. `mark.labelFormat` reuses a format preset. Overlapping labels are skipped. `mark.labelEnds` is `all`, `ends`, or `last` on a line. `mark.stackTotal` labels the total on a stacked bar or stacked area. `symbol`, `dataLabels`, `labels: "top"`, and `stackLabels` repair onto those keys. `axes.x`, `axes.y`, and `axes.y2` take `titlePosition` (`start`, `center`, `end`), `titleRotate` (degrees; default -90 or 90 on y and y2), `autoSkip` (false draws every tick; true skips crowded category labels instead of tilting them), `labelWidth` and `labelLines` (wrap, then ellipsize), `line` (true, false, or `{ show, color, width, dash }` of solid, dashed, or dotted), `tickMarks` (`inside`, `outside`, `none`), and `tickLength`. The baseline and tick marks are off until set. These draw on `createRenderer([line])`. `titleAnchor` repairs to `titlePosition`. `tickSize` repairs to `tickLength`.
- A bar splits series with `encoding.series`, or with `encoding.color` when that field is not `x`. `encoding.color` equal to `x` colours each bar and does not split series. `mark.stack` is `"stack"` or `"percent"`. `scale.type` `"log"` is a log axis. A temporal `x` is a time axis. `format` on an axis or channel is applied to the ticks. Rule, band, and text `annotations` are drawn. Tooltip, crosshair, zoom, pan, brush, animation, `legend.interactive`, and `a11y.keyboard` / `a11y.dataTable` are drawn by `@chartkitdev/core/interact` on the client (tooltip defaults on for line, bar, area, scatter, combo, donut, and waterfall. A waterfall hover card reads the bar under the pointer. Sankey nodes and links, and waterfall bars, are named on `pointclick`, `seriesclick`, and `interaction.select` via `data-ck-name`). `tooltip.fields` chooses the rows and their order: a string is a field name, and an object may set `title` and a `format` preset. `tooltip.position` is `auto` (above, then below, then beside), `top`, `bottom`, `left`, or `right`. `tooltip.crosshairLabel` prints the hovered x value on the guide. A fields string and the position synonyms `above`, `below`, `over`, and `under` are repaired. `interaction.select` is `"point"` or `"series"`. A click emits `pointclick` or `seriesclick` with `series`, `datum`, `index`, `x`, `y`, `value`, and the original `row`. Enter or Space on a focused point emits `pointclick`. Shift, Ctrl, or Meta adds to the selection. Escape or a background click clears it. `--ck-dim` fades the rest and `--ck-selected` strokes the chosen mark. Hovering a legend item highlights that series, and `legendclick` fires for the item. `select: true` repairs to `"point"`. `onClick` and `click` are removed, because events are not spec keys. The static SVG string stays the same, so SSR output does not include the tooltip. `validate` does not warn for these, including `interaction.select`. Keyboard, the data table, and legend clicks stay off unless set. The default theme is `auto` (Soft: `light-dark`, transparent plot, page scheme; optional card via `--ck-background`). `soft`, `refined`, and `editorial` are built in. `midnight` is opt-in. Other names stay midnight until imported. `--ck-*` or `--chart-N` still wins.

## Repair loop

1. `const result = validate(spec)`.
2. When `result.ok` is false, `repair(spec)` applies every safe JSON Patch in `fix` and returns `{ spec, ok, errors, warnings, applied }`. The input is not mutated.
3. Render the returned `spec` when `ok` is true. Otherwise read the remaining errors. Repair hints (CK1009) are sorted first. A missing or unknown `type` does not also list `metric`, OHLC, or `color` requirements from other chart types.

`repair` stops when the spec is valid, when a patch no longer applies, or after a few rounds. It does not invent fields.

Each example below is a minimal valid spec.

## line

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "line",
  "data": [
    { "quarter": "Q1", "units": 40 },
    { "quarter": "Q2", "units": 55 },
    { "quarter": "Q3", "units": 48 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "quarter", "y": "units" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Units peaked in Q2." }
}
```

## bar

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "bar",
  "data": [
    { "lane": "A", "stops": 12 },
    { "lane": "B", "stops": 7 },
    { "lane": "C", "stops": 15 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "lane", "y": "stops" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Lane C has the most stops." }
}
```

## pie

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "pie",
  "data": [
    { "wood": "Oak", "boards": 8 },
    { "wood": "Pine", "boards": 5 },
    { "wood": "Maple", "boards": 3 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "wood", "y": "boards" },
  "mark": { "labels": true, "padAngle": 1.5 },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Oak is the largest share of boards." }
}
```

## donut

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "donut",
  "data": [
    { "wood": "Oak", "boards": 8 },
    { "wood": "Pine", "boards": 5 },
    { "wood": "Maple", "boards": 3 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "wood", "y": "boards" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Oak is the largest share of boards." }
}
```

## stacked-area

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "stacked-area",
  "data": [
    { "year": "2022", "rail": 20, "road": 30 },
    { "year": "2023", "rail": 24, "road": 28 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "year", "y": ["rail", "road"] },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Road stayed larger than rail." }
}
```

## scatter

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "scatter",
  "data": [
    { "temp": 16, "yieldKg": 3 },
    { "temp": 22, "yieldKg": 5 },
    { "temp": 27, "yieldKg": 4 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "temp", "y": "yieldKg" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Yield is highest at 22 degrees." }
}
```

## combo

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "combo",
  "data": [
    { "week": "W1", "orders": 30, "rate": 0.4 },
    { "week": "W2", "orders": 36, "rate": 0.55 }
  ],
  "encoding": {
    "x": "week",
    "y": [
      { "field": "orders", "mark": "bar" },
      { "field": "rate", "mark": "line", "axis": "y2" }
    ]
  },
  "axes": { "y2": { "title": "Fill rate" } },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Orders and the fill rate both rose." }
}
```

## heatmap

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "heatmap",
  "data": [
    { "bin": "A", "band": "Low", "level": 1 },
    { "bin": "B", "band": "Low", "level": 4 },
    { "bin": "A", "band": "High", "level": 2 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "bin", "y": "band", "color": "level" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Bin B in the low band is the darkest cell." }
}
```

## gauge

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "gauge",
  "metric": { "label": "Capacity", "value": 64, "min": 0, "max": 100 },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Capacity is 64 out of 100." }
}
```

## kpi

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "kpi",
  "metric": { "label": "Tickets", "value": 18, "delta": -0.05 },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Open tickets are 18, slightly down." }
}
```

## sparkline

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "sparkline",
  "data": [4, 6, 5, 9, 8],
  "a11y": { "alt": "The sparkline ends higher than it starts." }
}
```

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "mini-area",
  "data": [2, 3, 3, 6, 5],

}
```


## spike

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "spike",
  "data": [
    { "slot": "t1", "hits": 0 },
    { "slot": "t2", "hits": 6 },
    { "slot": "t3", "hits": 1 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "slot", "y": "hits" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Hits spike at t2." }
}
```

## candlestick

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "candlestick",
  "data": [
    { "day": "D1", "open": 5, "high": 7, "low": 4, "close": 6 },
    { "day": "D2", "open": 6, "high": 6, "low": 3, "close": 4 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "day", "open": "open", "high": "high", "low": "low", "close": "close" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "The second session closed below its open." }
}
```

## histogram

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "histogram",
  "data": [
    { "score": 1 },
    { "score": 2 },
    { "score": 2 },
    { "score": 8 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "score" },
  "mark": { "bins": 2 },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Scores cluster at the low end." }
}
```

## boxplot

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "boxplot",
  "data": [
    { "group": "A", "value": 1 },
    { "group": "A", "value": 3 },
    { "group": "A", "value": 9 },
    { "group": "B", "value": 2 },
    { "group": "B", "value": 4 },
    { "group": "B", "value": 5 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "group", "y": "value" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Group A stretches higher than group B." }
}
```

## radar

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "radar",
  "data": [
    { "spoke": "Speed", "car": 4, "bike": 2 },

    { "spoke": "Ease", "car": 3, "bike": 4 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "spoke", "y": ["car", "bike"] },
  "a11y": { "alt": "The bike scores higher on cost and ease." }
}
```

```json
  "version": "1",
```

```json
    { "from": "Source", "to": "Mill", "flow": 10 },
    { "from": "Mill", "to": "Shop", "flow": 6 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "source": "from", "target": "to", "y": "flow" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "The mill sends flow on to the shop." }
}
```

## bullet

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "bullet",
  "data": [{ "name": "Revenue", "value": 275, "target": 250, "good": 300 }],
  "encoding": { "x": "name", "y": "value", "target": "target" },
  "mark": { "ranges": ["good"] },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Revenue is past its target." }
}
```

## waterfall

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "waterfall",
  "data": [
    { "step": "Open", "amount": 120, "total": true },
    { "step": "Won", "amount": 40 },
    { "step": "Close", "amount": 160, "total": true }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "step", "y": "amount" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "The close is 160." }
}
```

## area-range

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "area-range",
  "data": [
    { "month": "Jan", "revenue": 40, "lo": 36, "hi": 48 },
    { "month": "Feb", "revenue": 55, "lo": 46, "hi": 66 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "month", "y": "revenue", "low": "lo", "high": "hi" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Revenue is forecast inside a widening band." }
}
```

## bar-range

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "bar-range",
  "data": [
    { "month": "Jan", "min": -2, "max": 6 },
    { "month": "Jul", "min": 17, "max": 29 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "month", "low": "min", "high": "max" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "July ranges from 17 to 29." }
}
```

## errorbar

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "errorbar",
  "data": [{ "assay": "Glucose", "mean": 5.2, "lo": 4.9, "hi": 5.5 }],
  "encoding": { "x": "assay", "y": "mean", "low": "lo", "high": "hi" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Glucose is 5.2, from 4.9 to 5.5." }
}
```

## gantt

```json
{"version":"1","type":"gantt","data":[{"id":"a","task":"Spec","section":"Plan","start":"2026-03-02","end":"2026-03-13","status":"done"},{"id":"b","task":"Ship","start":"2026-04-06","milestone":true,"depends":"a"}],"a11y":{"alt":"Ship follows the spec."}}
```

## timeline

```json
{"version":"1","type":"timeline","data":[{"label":"Founded","date":"2014-06-01"},{"label":"Platform","start":"2024-01-01","end":"2026-01-01","kind":"period"}],"a11y":{"alt":"The company started in 2014."}}
```

## quadrant

```json
{"version":"1","type":"quadrant","quadrants":["Quick wins","Big bets","Fill-ins","Reconsider"],"data":[{"name":"SSO","x":0.2,"y":0.8},{"name":"Reports","x":0.8,"y":0.3}],"encoding":{"x":"x","y":"y"},"a11y":{"alt":"SSO is a quick win."}}
```

## venn

```json
{"version":"1","type":"venn","data":[{"set":"Search","size":12},{"set":"Filters","size":8},{"set":"Search+Filters","size":3}],"a11y":{"alt":"Search and filters overlap."}}
```

## journey

```json
{"version":"1","type":"journey","data":[{"section":"Pay","step":"Enter card","score":2,"actors":"Shopper"}],"a11y":{"alt":"Entering a card scores 2."}}
```

## React components (not the JSON spec)

`@chartkitdev/react` components take props. Those props are not the spec. Agents writing JSON should ignore this section. `<Chart spec={...} />` is the component that takes a spec.

| Component | Notable props (not spec keys) |
|---|---|
| `LineChart` | `data`, `series` or `dataKey`, `theme`, `responsive`, `curve` |
| `BarChart` | `data`, `dataKey`, `categoryKey`, `theme` |
| `DonutChart` | `data`, `dataKey`, `labelKey`, `theme` |
| `StackedArea` | `data`, `series`, `theme` |
| `ScatterChart` | `data`, `xKey`, `yKey`, `sizeKey`, `theme` |
| `ComboChart` | `data`, `xKey`, `leftAxis`, `rightAxis`, `theme` |
| `Heatmap` | `data`, `theme` |
| `GaugeChart` | `value`, `min`, `max`, `theme` |
| `KpiCard` | `label`, `value`, `delta`, `data`, `theme` |
| `Sparkline` | `data`, `theme`, `height` |
| `MiniArea` | `data`, `theme`, `height` |
| `ProgressRing` | `value`, `theme`, `size` |
| `SpikeChart` | `data`, `theme` |
| `CandlestickChart` | `data`, `theme`, `showVolume` |
| `Chart` | `spec` (the JSON object above), optional `render` |

## Other frameworks

`@chartkitdev/vue`, `@chartkitdev/svelte`, and `@chartkitdev/vanilla` render the same JSON spec through core. They do not add spec keys. Vue SSR and SvelteKit include the SVG. `mount(element, spec)` from `@chartkitdev/vanilla` returns `{ update(spec), destroy() }`, and `renderToString(spec)` is the SVG string core returns. The Svelte component uses `export let`, so Svelte 4 and Svelte 5 both compile it.
